The petitioner filed this petition U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1988 claiming compensation from the respondents due to injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

2. Brief facts of petitioner's case is that on 03.10.2022 at about 01.45 p.m, the petitioner was traveling in KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-3773, on Kolar-Bangalore NH Road, when the bus reached opposite to NH-75 Hotel, near Mylapura Gate Hosakote, Bangalore Rural District, the driver of said bus drove the same in a rash and negligent manner so as to endangering to human life and dashed to one Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-16/D-9498, which was parked on the road by its driver without any precaution, as a result of forced impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

3. Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Silicon City Hospital, wherein he took treatment as inpatient and wherein the duty doctors examined him clinically and radiologically, which revealed that he sustained Haemotama over forehead and all the injuries treated with conservatively and he has spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards medical expenses, food,
transportation, conveyance and other charges.

Due to the said accidental injuries, the petitioner completely bed ridden, cannot run, jump, cannot lift or carry any weight, unable to sleep properly,
she cannot do his activities as earlier to the accident and undergoing deep mental shock, pain and suffering, since the injuries caused permanent in nature.

Srinivasan.S vs K.S.R.T.C on 27 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171203603/
2 4.

It is contended that, this accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-3773 and also due to negligence on the part of the driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-16/D- 9498.

Hence, the Hosakote Police have registered a case against drivers of said vehicles in crime No.353/2022.
5.
It is contended that, prior to the accident the petitioner was hale, healthy, aged about 40 years and he was having own Printing Press and earning Rs.50,000/- p.m.
Due to accidental injuries he is not able to do her job and hence he lost his earning and suffering from mental shock and agony and also facing great financial difficulties.

6. The respondent No.1 being owner of the KSRTC Bus, Respondent No.2 being the RC owner of the Lorry, respondent No.3 being insurer of the Lorry and respondent No.4 is the insurance company of the Lorry
are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, this petition was filed against the respondents for claiming compensation.

7. In pursuance to the notice, the respondent No.1 to 4 appeared through their respective counsel and the respondent No.2 and 3 have filed joint written statement and the respondent No.1 and 4 have filed their written statements separately.

8. Brief contents of the written statement of respondent No.1 is that while admitting the ownership of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-3773, this respondent contended that, this accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-16/D-9498 as he was parked the Lorry in the middle of the road without any precautionary measurement and signals.
Hence, respondent No.2 to 4 are liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.

However,
on humanitarian ground this respondent paid the entire hospital bill amounting to Rs.26,206/- and same may be liable to be deducted and in case of holding contributory negligence on the part of the Lorry either fully or partially.
The insurer and owner of the lorry shall be directed to refund the medical expenses paid by this respondent to the petitioner to the extent of their liability.

Further, it has denied the date, place, mode of accident and nature of injuries, age, income, occupation of the petitioner, medical expenses incurred by her and disability caused to her and also contended that,
claim of the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition.

9. Brief contents of the written statement of respondent No.2 and 3 are that the petition filed by the petition is not maintainable neither under facts of the case nor under the question of law and it is to be dismissed in limine.

It is further contended that these respondents are the owner and driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-16/D-9498 who parked left side of the road and taken the required all safety and precautionary methods with due diligence, because of the negligent and rash driving of the driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-3773, this accident was happened and the Bus suddenly came to the footpath and hit the lorry, the driver of the said bus drove the same beyond speed limits in a negligent manner without applying breaks.

The petitioner has filed this false case against the respondent No.2 and 3 with malafide intention in view of getting higher compensation and as the respondent No.1 who is the manager of the KSRTC Bus is vicariously liable for the conduct of the bus driver, so, he being solely responsible for the compensation.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition against these respondents.

Srinivasan.S vs K.S.R.T.C on 27 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171203603/
3 10.
The respondent No.4 has contended in his written statement that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts of the case and denied the entire averments of the petition.

While admitting about issuance of insurance policy in respect of Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-16/
D-9498, this respondent restricted its liability to the terms and conditions of the policy.
Further contended that, driver of the said vehicle did not possess valid D.L. FC and permit as on the date of the accident and hence, terms and conditions of the insurance policy were violated.

It is contended that, this accident occurred due to sole rash and negligent driving of the driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-3773, as the driver of Lorry was parked his vehicle with all precautionary measures with signals to other vehicles.

Further these respondents denied the date, place and mode of accident, age, income and occupation of the petitioner, medical expenses incurred by him and disability caused to her and also contended that, claim of the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition with costs.
11.

On basis of the pleadings and materials, this tribunal framed the following:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that, on 03.10.2022 at about 01.45 p.m, the petitioner was traveling in a KSRTC bus bearing Reg No.KA-57/F-3773, proceeding on NH-75, when the bus reached near Mylapura Gate Opp. to NH-75 Hotel, Hosakote Taluk, Bangalore Rural District at that time, the driver of KSRTC Bus drove the same,
in a rash and negligent manner so as to endangering to human life, came at a high speed and dashed to one Parked Lorry bearing No.KA-16/D-9498 from behind,
which was parked with parking lights.
As a result of forced impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries?

2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, to what amount and from whom?
3. Whether order or award?
12.
In order to substantiate the case, petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 08 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.8.
On the other hand, the respondents have not examined any witnesses on their sides and no documents are marked before the Court.

13. Heard the arguments and perused the materials available on record.
14.

For the following reasons, I answer the above Issues as under:-
Issue No.1 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.4 : As per final order, for the following:

4
15 . Issue No.1:- The petitioner filed this petition under against respondents for claiming compensation due to injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

16. The petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and filed affidavit in lieu of chief examination and in his chief affidavit he had reiterated the averments of petition and got marked 08 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.8.

Ex.P.1 is the copy of F.I.R. Ex.P.2 is the copy of complaint, Ex.P.3 is the copy of spot mahazar, Ex.P.4 is the copy of sketch, Ex.P.5 is the copy of IMV report, Ex.P.6 is the copy of wound certificate, Ex.P.7 is the copy of charge sheet and Ex.P.8 is the notarized copy of Aadhaar card.

17. On perusal of Ex.P.4-spot sketch and Ex.P.7-charge sheet, it appears that, near Mylapura Gate Hosakote, opposite to NH-75 Hotel, Bangalore, the driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-3773 drove the same, in a rash and negligent manner came at high speed and dashed to one Lorry bearing No.KA-16/D-9498, which was parked on the road by its driver without any precautionary measures and caused the accident.

Hence, Hosakote Police filed Charge sheet against driver of the KSRTC Bus as A.1 and driver of Lorry as A.2.
18.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR(Civil) 319 Kausum and others V/s Satbir and others held that, in the petition for compensation U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act.1988 the petitioner has to prove the incident only on the preponderance of the probabilities and standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt is not required.
19.

sentences.text:
After careful scrutiny of Ex.P.1-F.I.R. Ex.P.2- complaint, Ex.P.3-spot mahazar, Ex.P.4-sketch,
Ex.P.5- IMV report, Ex.P.6-wound certificate and Ex.P.7-charge sheet, it appears that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-57/F-3773 and also due to negligence on the part of the driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-16/D-9498.
Accordingly, this Tribunal answer the Issue No.1 Partly in the Affirmative.
20. Issue No.2:- The petitioner claiming the compensation amount of Rs.5,00,000/- with respect to injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.
The petitioner produced wound certificate issued by Silicon City Hospital, Hosakote, Bangalore and prayed to award compensation amount.
The respondents not disputed the said documents.
On perusal of Ex.P.6 the wound certificate, it discloses that the petitioner has sustained Haematoma over the forehead.
The doctor opined that the above said injury is simple in nature.

Therefore, taking all these facts and nature of injury, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of Rs.15,000/- as reasonable compensation under the head of pain and suffering.
21. To prove the disability, neither the petitioner had examined his treated Doctor, nor produced any disability certificate, medical bills and not produced discharge summary.

Hence the petitioner is not entitled to claim any compensation amount under the head loss of income on account of permanent disability, medical expenditure, transportation, nourishment and conveyance charges and also future medical expenses.

Srinivasan.S vs K.S.R.T.C on 27 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171203603/
5 22.

The petitioner stated that, prior to the accident he was hale, healthy and aged about 40 years, he was having own Printing Press and earning Rs.50,000/- p.m. and due to injuries sustained in the accident, he is unable to attend his work and lost his earnings.
The petitioner had not produced any documents to prove his income and avocation.
The petitioner has sustained simple injury and not treated as an inpatient.
Hence, the petitioner is not entitled any compensation under the head loss of income during laid up period and also loss of amenities in life.

23. Considering the oral evidence coupled with documentary evidence, it is just and proper to grant compensation as follows:
 Under the Heads Amount 1. Pain and Sufferings Rs. 15,000/-
2.
Medical Expenses Rs. NIL 3. Transportation, Nourishment, NIL  Conveyance and

Attendant Rs.
 Charges.

4. Loss of Income during Laid-up Rs. NIL  Period.
5. Towards Loss of Amenities in Rs. NIL  Life  Total Rs. 15,000/-
As per the written statement of the respondent No.1 KSRTC, it appears that the respondent No.1 has already paid Rs.26,206/- as compensation.
Therefore, this Tribunal is of the opinion that in the interest of justice and equity, it is just and proper to award the said amount as a compensation.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.26,206/-.
24. Liability:-
The respondent No.1 is the RC owner-cum-Insurer of KSRTC bus bearing Reg No.KA-57/F-3773.

Respondent No.2 is the RC owner and Respondent No.3 is the i n s u r e d a n d r e s p o n d e n t N o . 4 i s t h e i n s u r e r o f t h e L o r r y b e a r i n g Reg.No.KA-16/D-9498.
25.

As already discussed in the Issue No.1 it is proved that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the KSRTC Bus driver and also due to negligent parking of Lorry by it's driver on the road.
Hence, the respondent No.1 and 4 jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Further, the counsel for the respondent No.1 filed memo by admitting the 50% of the liability and counsel for respondent No.4 has also admitted liability to the extent of 50%.

Hence, the Respondent No.1 being RC Owner-cum-Insurer of the KSRTC Bus and Respondent No.4 being Insurer of the Lorry are primarily held liable to pay the 50% each of the compensation amount with interest to the petitioner.

Srinivasan.S vs K.S.R.T.C on 27 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171203603/
6 26.
The respondent No.1 took contention that, already the interim compensation amount of Rs.26,206/- towards medical expenses has been paid.
This Tribunal has awarded the compensation only of Rs.26,206/-.
The liability of the respondent No.1 and 4 is 50% each.
Therefore, respondent No.4 is liable to repay the 50% compensation amount to the respondent No.1.
Hence, the respondent No.4 is liable to pay of Rs.13,103/- to the respondent No.1.
Accordingly, this Tribunal answered Issue No.2 in the Partly Affirmative.
27. Issue No.3:

For the foregoing reasons, this Tribunal proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby Partly allowed with cost as hereunder:
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.26,206/-.

Since, the entire amount has been paid by the respondent No.1, the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation from the respondents.
Respondent No.4 being the insurer of the Lorry is liable to pay Rs.13,103/- to the respondent No.1 within 60 days from the date of this order.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw the award accordingly.
